question: Could a withdrawal from my RDSP make me repay more in government grants or bonds than I actually withdraw?
generated_answer:
You may have to repay some or all of the government grants and bonds paid into your RDSP if you withdraw more than the Home Buyer Plan ($20,000) or the Life Saving Plan ($10,000) amounts, unless you qualify for the Disability Tax Credit (DTC) exemption. You may also have to repay some or all of the government grants and bonds if you are no longer eligible for the DTC. The amount of grants and bonds you may have to repay are calculated based on the formula that is part of the terms and conditions of the legislation. You may not have to repay all of the grants and bonds you have received if you are eligible for the DTC exemption. In order to be eligible for the DTC exemption, you must meet the following conditions:

- You are eligible for the DTC for 4 of the last 6 taxation years; or

- You are eligible for the DTC for 4 of the last 6 taxation years and have a terminal illness; or

- You are eligible for the DTC for 4 of the last 6 taxation years and are a beneficiary under a Registered Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP) or a Registered Retirement Income Fund (RRIF). If you are eligible for the DTC exemption, you may not have to repay all of the grants and bonds you have received. If you are not eligible for the DTC exemption, you may have to repay all of the grants and bonds you have received.
